title: Interleaved lifecycle guarantees and support catalog for LTS variants (runtime, API, SDK, Console)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: produce a single, consumable support catalog and orchestrated upgrade policy that defines guaranteed stability windows, inter-product compatibility contracts, and automated rollback triggers for LTS channel variants across the Serving Runtime, Redwood API, official SDKs, and Redwood Console. This ticket consolidates previous LTS artifacts into a canonical reference and specifies the tooling changes required to automate rollout gates and coordinated upgrades across surfaces.
scope: Include runtime (kernel selection, KV/cache compatibility), API surface (request/response schema and deprecation windows), official SDKs (Python, TS), and Console (dashboards, rollout controls). Exclude: third-party integrations not owned by Redwood and experimental model flavors outside curated LTS list.
acceptance_criteria: A single support catalog document published in Confluence that lists per-surface guarantees (bugfix vs security vs feature) and the supported co-existence combinations for active LTS releases.
A compatibility matrix file (CSV) checked into git that can be consumed by internal rollout tooling and the Console.
Rollout gating rules implemented in the release-orchestrator microservice that enforce: model/runtime compatibility, SDK version pin checks, and canary failure thresholds before global rollout.
Automated tests that simulate staggered upgrades across surfaces and assert rollback triggers fire when error-rate or latency SLOs exceed configured thresholds.
Documentation and runbook for on-call and customer success describing supported upgrade paths and recommended customer remediation steps.
proposed_support_matrix_summary:
(CSV-ready lines) surface, LTS-channel, min-compatible-versions, recommended-upgrade-window, guaranteed-security-backports
runtime, LTS-1, runtime-1.20+, api-2025.10+, sdk-python-2.3+, console-2025.11+, 90 days, security and critical bug backports for 12 months
api, LTS-1, api-2025.10+, runtime-1.20+, sdk-ts-1.8+, console-2025.11+, 90 days, contract stability: request schema stable for 6 months
sdk-python, LTS-1, sdk-python-2.3+, api-2025.10+, runtime-1.20+, 60 days, deprecation warnings for two release cycles
sdk-ts, LTS-1, sdk-ts-1.8+, api-2025.10+, 60 days, maintain backward compat for major features
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use 'channel contract' approach rather than strict version locking — define compatibility predicates instead of exact version lists to allow patch-level flexibility.
Trade-off: Predicates increase complexity in tooling but reduce customer force-upgrades during low-risk runtime patches.
Decision: Backport security fixes for 12 months for LTS channels; feature backports are opt-in and limited to high-impact regressions.
Trade-off: Longer backport windows increase maintenance cost for runtime team; offset with automated cherry-pick tooling and a small sustained support cadre.
notes: Initial draft of compatibility predicates created and stored at: https://confluence.redwood/team/release-ops/interleaved-lifecycle-draft
Runtime engineering prototyped a CSV export of kernel compatibility; see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1127
Console needs an endpoint to surface CSV rows as a table and to feed the rollout-orchestrator; RFC opened: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ZabcExample
Requested input from SDK leads (Emma Chen, Raj Patel) on minimum supported language runtimes; Emma prefers semantic-minor pinning, Raj prefers predicate-based signal.
implementation_plan:
1) Finalize catalog schema and compatibility predicate language (2 weeks)
2) Add CSV validator and schema to runtime repo, add CI job (2 weeks)
3) Implement rollout-orchestrator rules and failover hooks (3 sprints)
4) Console UI: table + single-click pause/rollback (1 sprint)
5) End-to-end smoke tests and cross-surface upgrade simulations (1 sprint)
6) Publish support catalog and runbook, announce to customers (1 week)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Mis-specified predicates could allow incompatible combinations into production. Mitigation: conservative defaults, strong test harness with staged combination permutations.
Risk: Increased maintenance burden for backports. Mitigation: automated cherry-pick bots and limited on-call rotation for LTS support.
Risk: Console rollout UI misuse could trigger premature rollbacks. Mitigation: RBAC gating and audit logs; require two-person approval for global rollbacks.
